purpose: Candidate sources for a later independently annotated transport-notice evaluation. This is not a real-text benchmark, a frozen holdout, or evidence of model performance.
selection_method: Machine-assisted search and source inspection; no human gold annotation has been completed.
scope: Official carrier notices about Europe-Asia ocean-network disruption or relevant endpoint/transfer-port disruption. None is an ASML internal document or proof that ASML cargo used an affected service.
independence_warning: Thirteen sources are not thirteen independent events. Related notices share event_group; distinct operational groups can still share a wider disruption. The ten operational event groups are not a claim of statistical independence.
split_policy: Keep every original, translation, amendment, syndication and linked operational update of one event together. Consider holding an entire correlation_group together when constructing a conservative external holdout. Freeze the selected dated version before evaluation.
text_capture_policy: Only titles, links, dates and short original paraphrases are stored. Full notice text and private contact information are not redistributed. Live pages can change, so this registry alone cannot support exact text replay.
mapping_policy: Do not translate calendar dates, voyage numbers, port closures, berth waiting times or a voyage slide into an NL_ocean add_lead change without an explicit service-to-route mapping, planning calendar and valid interpretation of the affected dispatches. Unknown amounts remain unknown.

sources.title: Capacity Adjustment Changes Far East Asia to Europe Services
sources.applicability_reason: The notice concerns an Asia-North Europe service, but provides no link between AE55 and the hypothetical Netherlands-to-Singapore spare-parts lane.
sources.paraphrase: Congestion prompted an AE55 voyage slide. The table identifies the first changed vessel, voyage identifiers and Shanghai departure timing.
unresolved_fields_for_model: lead-time change rather than sailing-date change

sources.title: Blanking Far East Asia to Med Services
sources.applicability_reason: A related Europe-Asia operational setting, but Mediterranean services and blank sailings do not establish a Netherlands-Singapore transit-time increment.
sources.paraphrase: Terminal congestion led to announced blank voyages on AE11 and AE15, with first affected vessels and departure dates listed.
unresolved_fields_for_model: whether blanking changes booking availability or transit time

sources.title: Voyage Slide - Far East Asia to Med Services
sources.applicability_reason: The notice supplies a concrete AE11 schedule amendment, but not an internal NL_ocean mapping or a general extra-transit duration.
sources.paraphrase: An AE11 sailing was shifted following port congestion; the amendment gives the first affected vessel, revised voyage identifiers and an August departure.

sources.title: North Europe Port Update
sources.applicability_reason: Relevant to European gateways and possible regional contingencies, but neither Rotterdam nor the hypothetical cargo's exact service and delay are specified.
sources.paraphrase: Several factors raised terminal congestion and disrupted vessel and barge schedules. Shipment-specific contingencies were to be communicated separately.
unresolved_fields_for_model: whether alternate European gateway is used

sources.title: Slow Operations at Hutchinson Port Delta II in Rotterdam
sources.date_notes: The page retains dated February and March updates. These versions describe one labour-disruption event and must not enter different splits.
sources.applicability_reason: The hypothetical origin country matches, but terminal usage by the assumed spare-parts lane is unknown. Reduced moves per hour are not a quantified extra-week transit delay.
sources.paraphrase: A strike and subsequent slowdown reduced terminal productivity. A later update reports restored capacity and cancellation of planned contingencies from week 13.
unresolved_fields_for_model: conversion from terminal productivity to lane capacity

sources.title: Customer advisory: Strike action of lashing companies in Rotterdam
sources.date_notes: Initial, extension and resumption notices are retained on the same page; they belong to one event group.
sources.applicability_reason: Directly concerns the assumed origin's ocean gateway, but it does not establish which bookings are affected or a fixed additional transit time for NL_ocean.
sources.paraphrase: Lashing work stopped, was extended without a fixed end date, and later resumed under court order. Backlogs and vessel contingencies persisted after resumption.
unresolved_fields_for_model: dispatch interval distinct from strike hours

sources.title: Customer Advisory – AE12 Voyage Slide
sources.applicability_reason: The notice is a real Asia-Europe schedule amendment, but its Adriatic service is not shown to serve the hypothetical Netherlands-Singapore lane.
sources.paraphrase: Operational problems in the Adriatic network triggered an AE12 voyage slide, with the first affected vessel and changed voyage numbers stated.
unresolved_fields_for_model: change in transit duration versus departure position

sources.title: Shipping between Asia and the South Europe? Here’s an important service update
sources.date_notes: The inspected English page does not expose an unambiguous publication date in its readable body. The September URL is not used as an exact publication date.
sources.applicability_reason: This changes an Asia-South Europe port order. It does not supply an NL_ocean lead-time increment or prove applicability to a Netherlands origin.
sources.paraphrase: SE1 temporarily placed Rijeka before Koper to address congestion, with the affected voyage range and revised port sequence identified.

sources.title: Maersk Asia Pacific Market Update - June 2024
sources.applicability_reason: The notice links diversions to Asia-Europe travel and Singapore congestion, but industry-wide figures cannot be assigned to the project's single lane or supply pool.
sources.paraphrase: Cape diversions lengthened voyages and tightened capacity. The update discusses congestion at Asian hubs and alternatives including air and sea-air transport.
unresolved_fields_for_model: lane-level capacity rather than industry estimates

sources.title: Update to Vessel blockage in the Suez Canal
sources.date_notes: The page displays 8 April 2021 and retains dated updates from 24 March through 20 April. A single exact original publication date is not inferred from the URL or conflicting page markers.
sources.applicability_reason: The event affected routes between European and Asian hubs, but vessel-specific status and changing updates cannot be collapsed into one extra-week value for all hypothetical dispatches.
sources.paraphrase: A sequence of updates covers canal blockage, rerouting, vessel queues and recovery. Effects vary across vessels and dates, and urgent cargo alternatives are discussed.
unresolved_fields_for_model: whether a quote is vessel-specific or network-wide

sources.title: CUSTOMER ADVISORY –NEMO SERVICE – Change of rotation in North Europe
sources.applicability_reason: The notice explicitly changes Rotterdam availability but a port omission is not an add_lead operation. Applicability to the hypothetical Singapore lane requires a service map and rerouting decision.
sources.paraphrase: CMA CGM extended a Rotterdam omission on NEMO. Customers were told to book imports and exports through other ports in the service rotation.
unresolved_fields_for_model: rerouting operation outside current delay-only schema

sources.title: Belgian National Strike Disrupts Port Operations and Logistics Chain
sources.date_notes: The page labels live-ticker updates rather than an unambiguous first publication date.
sources.applicability_reason: Antwerp could be a regional alternative gateway, but its use by the hypothetical supply chain is not established and no shipment-level delay magnitude is supplied.
sources.paraphrase: A strike stopped vessel traffic. A later update reports resumed movements while warning that congestion and a vessel backlog remained.

sources.title: East Asia network recovery: Update 3
sources.applicability_reason: The update describes regional network recovery without confirming impact on the assumed Netherlands-Singapore route. The notice offers no deterministic duration for the remaining intermittent delays.
sources.paraphrase: East Asian ports were recovering after typhoon disruption, but regional congestion and strong demand continued to cause intermittent delays on some trades.
